slides.headline: If your child is turning 3 soon, expect big feelings and even bigger opinions. Here are 5 things every parent should know.

slides.title: **"No" becomes their favorite word.**
body: They are testing a brand-new idea: I am a separate person with my own wants.
It is a sign of growth, not a sign that you are failing.
slides.say: "You can say no to the shoes. You cannot say no to staying safe. Which pair do you pick?"
slides.close: Choices give them power without giving them the steering wheel.

slides.title: **Feelings arrive faster than words.**
body: They feel it all, and cannot yet explain it.
Meltdowns are often a language problem in disguise.
slides.say: "You look so mad. You wanted the blue cup. I am right here."
slides.close: Name it first. Fix it second.

slides.title: **They suddenly want to do everything alone.**
body: Getting dressed takes 20 minutes. Pouring the milk makes a lake.
That is practice, and practice is messy.
slides.say: "Do you want to try first, or shall we do it together?"
slides.close: Extra time now saves you months of power struggles later.

slides.title: **Pretend play is doing real work.**
body: Feeding a teddy bear is rehearsing empathy, language and problem solving.
Join in for ten minutes and let them lead.
slides.say: "Oh no, teddy is hungry. What should we cook for him?"
slides.close: You do not need special toys. You need your attention.

slides.title: **Routine is their safety net.**
body: When the day feels predictable, they feel safe enough to cooperate.
A simple order for morning and bedtime does most of the work.
slides.say: "First pajamas, then book, then lights out. I will show you the pictures."
